chains.title: GATA2 motif loss at the LMO1 enhancer

links.claim: On the plus strand rs2168101 is C>A; because LMO1 is on the minus strand, this is G>T on the transcript strand, so the protective TATA allele corresponds to plus-strand alt A. Alt A reduces GATA2 binding at the rs2168101 sequence. GATA2 is the best-supported GATA factor here: it has an own QBiC-SELEX model (own_model), is the highest-expressed GATA factor in SK-N-SH (133.07 TPM), and an ENCODE GATA2 ChIP-seq peak in SK-N-SH contains the variant. The GATA QBiC-SELEX group shows alt binding less (effect -0.816), and the literature independently links rs2168101 to a GATA motif.

rs2168101 lies within EH38E1518342, a distal enhancer-like cCRE with DNase and H3K27ac signal in the LMO1 intron. The ENCODE cCRE z-scores are maxima across biosamples, so SK-N-SH-specific enhancer activity is not directly proven by this row.
The enhancer is assigned to LMO1 by proximity and Open Targets L2G; LMO1 is the strongest candidate gene at this locus (best L2G score 0.92), far above RIC3.
The relevant expression context is neuroblastoma SK-N-SH, where GATA2 is highly expressed, GATA2 occupies the variant-containing region, and LMO1 is a known neuroblastoma oncogenic co-regulator.

The literature supports the direction: the risk G allele is favoured in allelic-imbalance assays in tumours, conversion of the GATA motif to the protective TATA allele reduces neuroblastoma initiation, and the protective TATA allele reduces MYCN-driven tumour penetrance in zebrafish. Thus alt A is predicted to lower GATA2-dependent LMO1 expression and reduce neuroblastoma risk. This is not a direct human C>A GATA2-dependence experiment.

predictions: GATA2 occupies the rs2168101 enhancer in SK-N-SH.
The ref C allele shows stronger GATA2 binding than alt A.
Alt A associates with lower LMO1 enhancer activity/LMO1 expression and a less adrenergic, lower-risk neuroblastoma phenotype.
falsified_if: Allele-specific GATA2 binding at rs2168101 is absent or alt A binds more than ref C.
GATA2 occupancy at EH38E1518342 is not seen in SK-N-SH or is not allele-specific.
Editing ref C to alt A does not reduce LMO1 enhancer activity or LMO1 expression, or GATA2 depletion does not modify the effect.

chains.title: GATA3 motif loss at the LMO1 enhancer

links.claim: Alt A reduces GATA3 binding at the rs2168101 sequence. GATA3 has an own QBiC-SELEX model (own_model), is expressed at 51.82 TPM in SK-N-SH, and an ENCODE GATA3 ChIP-seq peak in SK-N-SH contains the variant. GATA3 is a plausible alternative GATA factor, but it is lower expressed than GATA2 and the literature does not identify GATA3 specifically at this motif.
rs2168101 lies within EH38E1518342, a distal enhancer-like cCRE with DNase and H3K27ac signal in the LMO1 intron. The ENCODE cCRE z-scores are maxima across biosamples, not SK-N-SH-specific.
The enhancer is assigned to LMO1 by proximity and Open Targets L2G; LMO1 is the strongest candidate gene at this locus.
SK-N-SH is a neuroblastoma expression context in which GATA3 is expressed and occupies the variant-containing region, and LMO1 is neuroblastoma-relevant.

If GATA3 rather than GATA2 is the relevant GATA factor, alt A is predicted to reduce GATA3-dependent LMO1 expression and reduce neuroblastoma risk by analogy to the GATA-to-TATA protective-allele literature. This factor-specific phenotype is not directly tested.

predictions: GATA3 occupies the rs2168101 enhancer in SK-N-SH and shows allele-specific binding.
The ref C allele shows stronger GATA3 binding than alt A.
GATA3 perturbation changes LMO1 enhancer activity or expression.
falsified_if: GATA3 does not occupy the locus in SK-N-SH or shows no allele-specific binding.
GATA3 depletion does not alter LMO1 enhancer activity or LMO1 expression.
Allele-specific GATA3 binding is absent or alt A binds more than ref C.

grades_final.reason: H1 uses GATA2 because E10 is the GATA2 own-model QBiC-SELEX result (best model, effect -0.816, alt binds less), E18 shows GATA2 ChIP occupancy at the variant in SK-N-SH, and E06f/E20a independently describe rs2168101 as affecting a GATA motif. Allele orientation is consistent: plus-strand C>A corresponds to transcript-strand G>T given LMO1 is on the minus strand. The binding evidence is strong but not a direct allele-specific cellular GATA2 binding assay.
E03 directly places rs2168101 in EH38E1518342, a dELS with DNase and H3K27ac signal; the claim correctly notes that these z-scores are maxima across biosamples, not SK-N-SH-specific proof.
E02 places the variant in the LMO1 gene body 34.9 kb from the TSS, and E05 gives the strongest L2G score to LMO1 (0.92), far above RIC3.
E10 shows GATA2 is highly expressed in the SK-N-SH context (133.07 TPM), E18 shows GATA2 occupancy at the variant in SK-N-SH, and the cited literature supports LMO1 as neuroblastoma-relevant.

E20b-E20d and E06f-E06g strongly support the protective TATA/alt-A direction and reduced neuroblastoma initiation/penetrance, and E20c-E20d support allelic imbalance favoring the risk G/ref-C allele. However, the GATA2-specific dependence of the phenotype is inferred rather than directly tested in a human C>A GATA2 perturbation experiment.

GATA3 is an own-model member of the GATA group in E10 and is expressed in SK-N-SH, and E19 shows a GATA3 ChIP peak containing the variant in SK-N-SH. But the quoted QBiC-SELEX effect is the group best-model GATA2 effect; GATA3 is only listed as a passing member with the same sign, and there is no GATA3-specific allele-specific binding assay or literature linking GATA3 specifically to this motif. This is weak, not direct, support for GATA3 allele-specific binding.

E02 places the variant in the LMO1 gene body 34.9 kb from the TSS, and E05 gives the strongest L2G score to LMO1 (0.92), far above RIC3.

The phenotype claim is explicitly hypothetical for GATA3 and relies on analogy to the general GATA-to-TATA protective-allele literature. The cited evidence supports the general allele direction but does not test GATA3-specific dependence of LMO1 expression or neuroblastoma risk.
